snip.t: | Acute interstitial nephritis (AIN) | Recent drug (penicillins, PPIs, NSAIDs) or infection; fever, rash, eosinophilia; white‑cell casts | Eosinophiluria on Hansel stain; urine may be sterile; FeNa variable but often >1 %. |
| Acute interstitial nephritis | Drug exposure, eosinophilia, rash, fever | Steroid responsive; dialysis only for severe AKI features |
Look‑alike conditions: differentiate pyelonephritis from renal colic (flank pain + hematuria, no systemic signs) and from acute interstitial nephritis (eosinophilia, rash, recent drug).

qs.q: Which of the following is a typical finding in the urinalysis of a patient with acute interstitial nephritis?
o: Heavy proteinuria and red blood cell casts
White blood cells, red blood cells, and white cell casts
Sterile pyuria with no white blood cells
qs.e: The characteristic urine sediment in acute interstitial nephritis reveals white blood cells, red blood cells, and white cell casts. Heavy proteinuria is not typical, and the presence of WBCs distinguishes it from sterile pyuria without casts.
